                    text: [32m'# Typesense filter_by Syntax and Examples\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-07, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/tips-for-filtering.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Add your placeholder characters to the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'parameter in the collection schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. When adding documents, identify fields that might be empty and replace the empty or null values with your chosen placeholder (e.g.,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## # Filtering Nested Object Fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also filter on nested object fields by using the dot (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m') notation to refer to nested fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## # Filtering Nested Array Objects\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When filtering on fields inside nested array objects, you need to use a special syntax to ensure the filters are applied to the same object within the array. The syntax is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<nested_field_parent>.{<filter_conditions>}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, consider a menu collection with the following schema:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "name": "menu",\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "name", "type": "string"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients", "type": "object[]"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients.name", "type": "string[]"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients.concentration", "type": "int32[]"}\n'[39m +
                      [32m' ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "enable_nested_fields": true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'as array fields, despite being single valued.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can use any valid filter operators inside the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…'[39m
                  },

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense filter_by Syntax and Examples\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-07, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/tips-for-filtering.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## # Filtering Nested Object Fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also filter on nested object fields by using the dot (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m') notation to refer to nested fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, if you have a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'nested object inside your collection schema that looks like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You can filter by the customer's name like:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When filtering on fields inside nested array objects, you need to use a special syntax to ensure the filters are applied to the same object within the array. The syntax is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<nested_field_parent>.{<filter_conditions>}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, consider a menu collection with the following schema:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "name": "menu",\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "name", "type": "string"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients", "type": "object[]"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients.name", "type": "string[]"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients.concentration", "type": "int32[]"}\n'[39m +
                      [32m' ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "enable_nested_fields": true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To filter for dishes that have cheese with concentration less than 50, use:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter_by=ingredients.{name:=cheese && concentration:<50}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'object[]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Search does not work on deeply nested array of objects · Issue #1403 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|## TL;DR the search is effective at the first level of nesting but does not work on the second level.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Description Search does not work when specific fields of nested objects are indexed -- Both\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` items ``` and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` items.nested_items ``` are array of objects.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` { "facet": false, "index": true, "infix": false, "locale": "", "name": "items.name", "optional": true, "sort": false, "type": "string[]" }, { "facet": false, "index": true, "infix": false, "locale": "", "name": "items.nested_items.name", "optional": true, "sort": false, "type": "string[]" } ``` however, it **works** when the entire object is indexed -\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Collections API\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-08-03, last updated: 2026-08-08, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/collections.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense supports indexing nested objects (and array of objects) from `v0.24`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You must first enable nested fields at a collection level via the `enable_nested_fields` schema property, and the `object` or `object[]` data type:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl -k "http://localhost:8108/collections" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-H "X-TYPESENSE-API-KEY: ${TYPESENSE_API_KEY}" -d \'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "docs",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"enable_nested_fields": true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{"name": "person", "type": "object"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{"name": "details", "type": "object[]"}\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m"}'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you now search on an object field name, all sub-fields will be automatically searched.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use a dot notation to refer to specific sub-fields, e.g. `person.last_name` or `person.school.name`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To index specific fields inside an array of objects, you want to specify an **array data type**.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Indexing nested objects via flattening**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also flatten objects and arrays of objects into top-level keys before sending the data into Typesense.'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Tips for Searching Common Types of Data - Typesense\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense v0.24.0 supports nested objects and arrays of objects natively.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To enable nested fields, you'll need to use the\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'enable_nested_fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property when creating the collection, along with the\n'[39m +

                      [32m'object\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Important Side Note:** You can still send nested objects into Typesense, in fields not mentioned in the schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense specifically does not support *indexing*, *searching* or *filtering* nested objects, or arrays of objects.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We plan to add support for this shortly as part of (#227 (opens new window)).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In the meantime, you would have to flatten objects and arrays of objects into top-level keys before sending the data into Typesense.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also filter on nested object fields by using the dot (\n'[39m +

                      [32m'## # Filtering Nested Array Objects\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When filtering on fields inside nested array objects, you need to use a special syntax to ensure the filters are applied to the same object within the array. The syntax is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<nested_field_parent>.{<filter_conditions>}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'collection has a singular reference field type, we will only return the joined documents in an array when it has relation with more than one documents.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'strategy: nest_array\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'to force Typesense to return the joined documents in an array regardless of their relation count.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"By default, when we join on a collection, the collection's fields are returned as a nested document.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"In a one-to-many join query, you might want the joined collection's fields to be always represented as an array of objects, even if there is only a single match.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'"filter_by": "$books(id:*)",\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +

            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +

            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +

            [32m'</example>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use the gh command via the executeCommand tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel using the executeCommand tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:\n'[39m +

          name: [32m'newTask'[39m,
          description: [32m'Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.\n'[39m +
            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.                       [32m'2. When adding documents, identify fields that might be empty and replace the empty or null values with your chosen placeholder (e.g.,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## # Filtering Nested Object Fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also filter on nested object fields by using the dot (\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## # Filtering Nested Array Objects\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When filtering on fields inside nested array objects, you need to use a special syntax to ensure the filters are applied to the same object within the array. The syntax is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<nested_field_parent>.{<filter_conditions>}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, consider a menu collection with the following schema:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients.name", "type": "string[]"},\n'[39m +

                      [32m' ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "enable_nested_fields": true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'as array fields, despite being single valued.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can use any valid filter operators inside the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…'[39m

                      [32m'created: 2026-08-03, last updated: 2026-08-08, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/collections.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We call this definition the collection's `schema`, which is just a fancy term to describe the fields (and their data types) in your documents.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are two ways to specify a schema:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you have a case where you do want to index all fields in the document, except for a few fields, you can use the `{"index": false, "optional": true}` settings to exclude fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Note: it is not currently possible to have a mandatory field excluded from the indexing, hence the setting to optional.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Support for nested objects · Issue #19 · typesense/gatsby-plugin-typesense\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Typesense supports indexing nested objects and arrays of objects since v0.24: https://typesense.org/docs/guide/tips-for-searching-common-types-of-data.html#nested-objects.\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense filter_by Syntax and Examples\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-07, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/tips-for-filtering.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## # Filtering Nested Object Fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also filter on nested object fields by using the dot (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m') notation to refer to nested fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, if you have a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'nested object inside your collection schema that looks like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You can filter by the customer's name like:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When filtering on fields inside nested array objects, you need to use a special syntax to ensure the filters are applied to the same object within the array. The syntax is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<nested_field_parent>.{<filter_conditions>}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, consider a menu collection with the following schema:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "name": "menu",\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "name", "type": "string"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients", "type": "object[]"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients.name", "type": "string[]"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m' {"name": "ingredients.concentration", "type": "int32[]"}\n'[39m +
                      [32m' ],\n'[39m +
                      [32m' "enable_nested_fields": true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To filter for dishes that have cheese with concentration less than 50, use:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter_by=ingredients.{name:=cheese && concentration:<50}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'object[]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Search does not work on deeply nested array of objects · Issue #1403 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-11-29, last updated: 2025-05-19, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/1403)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|## TL;DR the search is effective at the first level of nesting but does not work on the second level.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Description Search does not work when specific fields of nested objects are indexed -- Both\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` items ``` and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` items.nested_items ``` are array of objects.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` { "facet": false, "index": true, "infix": false, "locale": "", "name": "items.name", "optional": true, "sort": false, "type": "string[]" }, { "facet": false, "index": true, "infix": false, "locale": "", "name": "items.nested_items.name", "optional": true, "sort": false, "type": "string[]" } ``` however, it **works** when the entire object is indexed -\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` { "name": "items", "type": "object[]" }, { "name": "items.nested_items", "type": "object[]" } ```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Defaulting to different type on nested objects · Issue #1882 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-08-08, last updated: 2025-03-15, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/1882)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'object[] will index all these fields, but will create the schema with int64[].\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'object[]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'int64[]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'CA: 2.5,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'EU: 5,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'GB: 5,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'US: 75,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Yes, given the following object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"currencies": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"AU": 2.5.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"EU": 5\n'[39m +
                      [32m'you can define the types for the children of currencies like this in the field schema definition:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'currencies\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Collections API\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-08-03, last updated: 2026-08-08, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/collections.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense supports indexing nested objects (and array of objects) from `v0.24`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You must first enable nested fields at a collection level via the `enable_nested_fields` schema property, and the `object` or `object[]` data type:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl -k "http://localhost:8108/collections" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-H "X-TYPESENSE-API-KEY: ${TYPESENSE_API_KEY}" -d \'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"name": "docs",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"enable_nested_fields": true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"fields": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{"name": "person", "type": "object"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{"name": "details", "type": "object[]"}\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m"}'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you now search on an object field name, all sub-fields will be automatically searched.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use a dot notation to refer to specific sub-fields, e.g. `person.last_name` or `person.school.name`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To index specific fields inside an array of objects, you want to specify an **array data type**.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Indexing nested objects via flattening**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also flatten objects and arrays of objects into top-level keys before sending the data into Typesense.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Tips for Searching Common Types of Data - Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-08, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/tips-for-searching-common-types-of-data.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense v0.24.0 supports nested objects and arrays of objects natively.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To enable nested fields, you'll need to use the\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'enable_nested_fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property when creating the collection, along with the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'object\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Important Side Note:** You can still send nested objects into Typesense, in fields not mentioned in the schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense specifically does not support *indexing*, *searching* or *filtering* nested objects, or arrays of objects.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We plan to add support for this shortly as part of (#227 (opens new window)).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In the meantime, you would have to flatten objects and arrays of objects into top-level keys before sending the data into Typesense.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, a document like this containing nested objects:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'would need to be flattened as:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"nested_field.field1": "value1",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"nested_field.field2": ["value2", "value3", "value4"],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"nested_field.field3.fieldA": "valueA",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"nested_field.field3.fieldB": ["valueB", "valueC", "valueD"]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'before indexing it into Typesense.'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Search does not work on deeply nested array of objects · Issue #1403\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-11-28, last updated: 2025-05-19, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/1403)\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +

            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response.             [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes.             [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use the gh command via the executeCommand tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.\n'[39m +

          description: [32m'Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.\n'[39m +
            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
